---
title: Flows
description: Understand flows, the core unit of orchestration in Prefect.
keywords: ["flow", "workflow", "orchestration"]
---

A flow is the most basic Prefect object. It is a container for workflow logic and
is the entrypoint that Prefect observes and orchestrates. Any Python function can
become a flow by adding the `@flow` decorator.

## Write a flow

Decorate a function with `@flow` to turn it into a flow:

{/* pmd-metadata: notest */}
```python
from prefect import flow


@flow
def my_flow():
    print("Hello from a flow!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    my_flow()
```

When the function runs, Prefect creates a flow run: a representation of a single
execution of the flow that is tracked whether you run locally, on your own
infrastructure, or on Prefect Cloud.

## Flows and tasks

Flows can call [tasks](/v3/concepts/tasks) to break work into observable,
retryable units. A flow that orchestrates other flows is called a subflow. See
[deployments](/v3/concepts/deployments) for how to schedule and run flows
remotely.

<Note>
  A function can be both readable and observable: the `@flow` decorator does not
  change how the function is called, it only adds orchestration around it.
</Note>

## Why flows matter

Because a flow is just a decorated function, the same code runs unchanged in an
open source deployment or against Prefect Cloud. This keeps local development and
production behavior consistent while Prefect adds retries, state tracking, and
logging around your existing logic.
